descriptionChirho: A heap of ashes, dung, or refuse, often used as a symbol of extreme poverty or degradation (1 Sam 2:8, Ps 113:7, Lam 4:5). All three clusters share identical semantic content: the determined singular (eng: the-Dung, spa: el-muladar, arb: الدِّمنَةِ, kor: 그-재더미, swa: takataka), the prepositional form with min (eng: from-the-ash-heap, spa: del-muladar, arb: مِنَ-المَزبَلَة, hin: कूड़े-से, swa: kutoka-jalani), and the plural (eng: ash-heaps, spa: muladares, arb: الْمَزَابِلَ, kor: 쓰레기-더미들, swa: jalala). Translations uniformly point to waste/refuse piles.
